'''Robert Gribben Hill''' (15 July 1938 — 19 November 2017) was a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] first-class [[cricket]]er and administrator.

Hill was born in at [[Kilmarnock]] in July 1938 and was educated there at [[Kilmarnock Academy]]. A [[club cricket]]er for Kilmarnock Cricket Club,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wdcu.co.uk/bobby-hill-kilmarnock-cc/|title=Bobby Hill (Kilmarnock CC)|publisher=www.wdcu.co.uk|date=20 November 2017|accessdate=11 July 2022}}</ref> he made his debut for [[Scotland national cricket team|Scotland]] in [[first-class cricket]] against [[Warwickshire County Cricket Club|Warwickshire]] at [[The Grange Club|Edinburgh]] in 1963, with Hill making two further appearances in that year against the touring [[Pakistan Eaglets cricket team|Pakistan Eaglets]] and [[Ireland cricket team|Ireland]]. He made three further appearances in first-class cricket for Scotland, against Warwickshire on Scotland's 1964 and 1965 tours of England, and finally against [[Surrey County Cricket Club|Surrey]] at [[The Oval]] on Scotland's 1969 tour of England.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/27/27036/First-Class_Matches.html|title=First-Class Matches played by Bobby Hill|publisher=CricketArchive|accessdate=11 July 2022|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Playing as a batsman in the Scottish side, Hill scored 105 runs in his six first-class matches at an [[batting average (cricket)|average]] of 11.66;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/27/27036/f_Batting_by_Team.html|title=First-Class Batting and Fielding For Each Team by Bobby Hill|publisher=CricketArchive|accessdate=11 July 2022|url-access=subscription}}</ref> he made one half century, a score of 50 against Warwickshire in 1964.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/26/26903.html|title=Warwickshire v Scotland, 1964|publisher=CricketArchive|accessdate=11 July 2022|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

After finishing his playing career, Hill served as the manager of the Scottish cricket team in the late 1990s, managing the team at the [[1997 ICC Trophy]] and the [[1999 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricketscotland.com/former-scotland-player-bobby-hill-dies/|title=Former Scotland Player Bobby Hill Dies|first=Lizzie|last=Sleet|publisher=www.cricketscotland.com|accessdate=11 July 2022}}</ref> Hill was also Chairman of Selectors for the Scottish national team, and served on the first board of [[Cricket Scotland]], which had replaced the Scottish Cricket Union in April 2001.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/news/12169392.limited-company-signals-brave-new-world-for-scottish-cricket/|title=Limited company signals brave new world for Scottish cricket|date=28 April 2001|work=[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]]|accessdate=11 July 2022}}</ref> Outside of cricket, he was a research chemist. Hill died at Kilmarnock in November 2017.<ref>{{cite book |title=Wisden Cricketers' Almanack 2018|first=Lawrence|last=Booth|date=2018|publisher=[[Bloomsbury Publishing]]|page=205|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TQlbEAAAQBAJ|isbn=9781472953544|language=en}}</ref>
